instruction: Write `examplemod.mixins.json`: common mixins in the package com.example.examplemod.mixin, CLIENT-only mixins in com.example.examplemod.mixin.client, refmap `examplemod.refmap.json`, Mixin 0.8.7, JAVA_21 compatibility, require=1. Explain why client mixins must go into the `client` section on a NeoForge dedicated server.
golden_reference:
{
  "required": true,
  "minVersion": "0.8.5",
  "package": "com.example.examplemod.mixin",
  "compatibilityLevel": "JAVA_21",
  "refmap": "examplemod.refmap.json",
  "injectors": {
    "defaultRequire": 1
  },
  "mixins": [
    "PlayerMixin",
    "LivingEntityMixin",
    "MobAccessor",
    "EntityInvoker"
  ],
  "client": [
    "client.MinecraftMixin"
  ],
  "server": []
}

/*
 * Why: classes listed under "mixins" are applied on BOTH logical sides. A mixin whose target
 * is a client-only class (e.g. net.minecraft.client.gui.Gui) cannot even be CLASS-LOADED on a
 * dedicated server - the target class is missing, so the mixin application crashes the server.
 * The "client" section defers application until the client-side mixin environment runs.
 */

  "root_cause": "@ModifyVariable without argsOnly=true scans LOCAL VARIABLES of the target method; at @At("RETURN") the int locals available do not uniquely/deterministically match the selector (no ordinal, no explicit name given), so the discriminator finds no candidate. The intent is to modify the int PARAMETER, which requires argsOnly.",
  "fix_explanation": "Add argsOnly = true and keep the @At("HEAD") injection point plus ordinal = 0 so the first int argument (`food`) is selected deterministically.",
  "code_patch": "@ModifyVariable(
        method = "eat(IF)V",
        at = @At("HEAD"),
        argsOnly = true,
        ordinal = 0)
private int examplemod$doubleFood(int food) { return food * 2; }"
}

In ONE self-contained file: (1) class ModEntities with DeferredRegister on ForgeRegistries.ENTITY_TYPES registering 'forest_wisp' (MobCategory.MONSTER, sized 0.8F x 1.8F, EntityType.Builder.of(ForestWisp::new, ...).build("forest_wisp")) and register(IEventBus); (2) a MOD-bus subscriber with @SubscribeEvent handlers for EntityAttributeCreationEvent (put the wisp with Monster.createMonsterAttributes(): MAX_HEALTH 24.0, MOVEMENT_SPEED 0.28) and SpawnPlacementRegisterEvent (register ON_GROUND / MOTION_BLOCKING_NO_LEAVES placement using ForestWisp::checkWispSpawnRules with Operation.REPLACE); (3) package-private ForestWisp extends Monster with the static createAttributes() builder and a static checkWispSpawnRules(EntityType, LevelAccessor, MobSpawnType, BlockPos, RandomSource) that delegates to Monster.checkMonsterSpawnRules and requires Y >= 40.
context: Mod id: examplemod. Platform: Minecraft Forge 1.20.1. Entity attributes are bound through EntityAttributeCreationEvent on the mod bus; spawn placements through SpawnPlacementRegisterEvent (net.minecraftforge.event.entity).

instruction: Forge 1.20.1 (mod id 'examplemod'). In ONE self-contained file, write ModFluids: register a FluidType 'myst' (density 1100, viscosity 1500, temperature 320) via DeferredRegister on ForgeRegistries.Keys.FLUID_TYPES; register source and flowing ForgeFlowingFluid (Source/Flowing) via DeferredRegister on ForgeRegistries.FLUIDS; register a LiquidBlock 'myst' (mapColor WATER, noCollission, strength 100.0F, noLootTable) and a BucketItem 'myst_bucket' (craftRemainder BUCKET, stacksTo 1); bind everything through one static ForgeFlowingFluid.Properties (slopeFindDistance 2, tickRate 10). Provide register(IEventBus). The FluidType + ForgeFlowingFluid stack is the Forge 1.20.1 API - BaseFlowingFluid is NeoForge-only.
context: Mod id: examplemod. Platform: Minecraft Forge 1.20.1. ForgeFlowingFluid.Properties takes (Supplier<FluidType>, supplier of source, supplier of flowing) and chain-configures block/bucket; suppliers are evaluated at registry time so declaration order is safe.

instruction: Forge 1.20.1 capstone (mod id 'examplemod'). In ONE self-contained file, write ModItems that combines three Forge 1.20.1 subsystems: (1) a ForgeConfigSpec IntValue MAX_CHARGE ('maxCharge', default 1000, range 1..1,000,000) declared in a static initializer; (2) a nested BatteryItem (stacksTo 1) whose appendHoverText appends the translatable 'tooltip.examplemod.battery.max' with the config value substituted (MAX_CHARGE.get()) styled ChatFormatting.GOLD; (3) a custom CreativeModeTab 'main' (DeferredRegister on the vanilla CREATIVE_MODE_TAB key) titled 'itemGroup.examplemod', iconed with the battery, displaying it via displayItems. Wire ITEMS and TABS registers through register(IEventBus). No NeoForge APIs.
context: Mod id: examplemod. Platform: Minecraft Forge 1.20.1. Config holders are read at tooltip time; creative tab items are accepted through the output callback.

instruction: Port this Forge 1.20.1 multi-file slice to NeoForge 1.21.1. The slice defines two items and a creative tab. Keep every top-level type name, field name and file path stable; preserve the creative-tab contents and registry identifiers exactly. Replace the Forge-only registry/event plumbing with the NeoForge 1.21.1 equivalents (registry keys from net.minecraft.core.registries.Registries, constructor-injected mod bus where needed). Return the complete NeoForge 1.21.1 file set for the slice.

Port this Forge 1.20.1 networking slice to NeoForge 1.21.1. The slice declares a SimpleChannel and one client-to-server message carrying an energy value. Migrate the transport to the NeoForge 1.21.1 payload API (CustomPacketPayload + StreamCodec + PayloadRegistrar via RegisterPayloadHandlersEvent), keeping the type name UpdateEnergyPacket, the field name energy, the wire format (varint) and the server-side handling behavior unchanged. Return the complete NeoForge 1.21.1 file set.

Port this Forge 1.20.1 player-tick handler to NeoForge 1.21.1. The handler heals the player by one food point every 200 ticks. NeoForge 1.21.1 split the tick events: use the dedicated PlayerTickEvent.Post event from net.neoforged.neoforge.event.tick instead of the phased TickEvent.PlayerTickEvent, keep the game-bus subscription, keep the numeric behavior identical, and keep the type name PlayerTickHandler. Return the complete NeoForge 1.21.1 file set.

Port this Forge 1.20.1 config slice to NeoForge 1.21.1. The slice declares a COMMON config with one integer and one boolean option and registers it from the mod constructor. Use the NeoForge 1.21.1 config spec type, keep the type name TaskConfig, the field names MAX_CHARGE / ALLOW_WIRELESS / SPEC, the config keys maxCharge / allowWireless, the defaults and the bounds unchanged. Return the complete NeoForge 1.21.1 file set.

Port this Forge 1.20.1 battery-item slice to NeoForge 1.21.1. The battery currently stores its charge in item NBT via getOrCreateTag. Migrate the item to the 1.20.5+ data component system: register an integer DataComponentType in a new ModDataComponents class, move the energy default into the item properties, replace all NBT access with component access, and adapt the tooltip override to the new 1.21.1 signature. Keep type names and the visual behavior (energy bar, tooltip text) identical. Registration order matters: data components must be registered before items. Return the complete NeoForge 1.21.1 file set including the new ModDataComponents file.

Port this Forge 1.20.1 container slice to NeoForge 1.21.1. The slice wires an EntityBlock to a MenuProvider BlockEntity, an AbstractContainerMenu and a client screen. NeoForge 1.21.1 changed several links of this chain: the container factory now receives RegistryFriendlyByteBuf, the client registers screens through RegisterMenuScreensEvent instead of a client-setup callback, and the block interaction method is useWithoutItem instead of use. Keep all type names and file paths stable and preserve the open-menu behavior. Return the complete NeoForge 1.21.1 file set.

Port this Forge 1.20.1 command-and-interaction slice to NeoForge 1.21.1. The slice registers a /task_energy command with a permission check and handles right-click-block events with an action-bar message. Keep both handler behaviors identical, keep the type name TaskCommands, and move the subscription to the correct NeoForge game bus. Return the complete NeoForge 1.21.1 file set.

Port this Forge 1.20.1 entity slice to NeoForge 1.21.1. The slice registers a custom golem entity type and attaches its attributes through EntityAttributeCreationEvent. Migrate the registry to the vanilla registry key from net.minecraft.core.registries.Registries and the holder type to DeferredHolder, keep the entity type name task_golem, the sized(0.6F, 1.8F) bounds and the monster attribute set identical. Return the complete NeoForge 1.21.1 file set.

Port this Forge 1.20.1 spawn-placement slice to NeoForge 1.21.1. The slice registers ground spawn placement for the custom golem through SpawnPlacementRegisterEvent. NeoForge 1.21.1 renamed the event to RegisterSpawnPlacementsEvent, and vanilla renamed the SpawnPlacements holder class to SpawnPlacementTypes in 1.20.5. Keep the placement type (ON_GROUND), the heightmap, the spawn predicate and the REPLACE operation identical, and keep the type name TaskSpawning. Return the complete NeoForge 1.21.1 file set.

Port this Forge 1.20.1 block-entity slice to NeoForge 1.21.1. The charger block entity persists one integer field. Minecraft changed the persistence contract in 1.20.5: load(CompoundTag) became loadAdditional(CompoundTag, HolderLookup.Provider) and saveAdditional(CompoundTag) gained the same provider parameter. Migrate the persistence methods, migrate the block entity type registration to the vanilla registry key and DeferredHolder, and keep the field name storedEnergy, the tag key StoredEnergy and the clamp behavior identical. Return the complete NeoForge 1.21.1 file set.
